reason: The cited evidence (E1) only reports elastic isotropy, phase stability, and softening resistance up to 900 °C, with no data on cold rolling, aging, dislocation structures, thermal expansion mismatch, or internal stresses. None of the key premises are supported by the cited passage.
premises: Cold rolling and aging introduce dislocation networks and sub-grain interfaces in HfNbTaTiZr.
Differential thermal expansion at these interfaces generates internal residual stresses.
These residual stresses modulate dislocation pinning and lattice stiffness.
This modulation unifies changes in creep rate, hardness, and elastic moduli across temperature.
The effect is operative from 293 K to 1250 °C and is stronger in cold-rolled/aged states.
